title: Let agents review code so people only check risky changes
summary: The Claude Code team says merged changes more than doubled from June to September while reverts fell over 40%, after moving most code reading to Claude reviewers.
agent_role: Claude runs tests and builds, a second agent reviews each change, parallel agents hunt bugs with verifiers voting, and a classifier decides whether zero, one or two people must approve. Humans handle risky paths and watch releases.
outcome: The team reports merged pull requests more than doubled from June to September while the share reverted fell by more than 40 percent.
what_they_did: Anthropic's Claude Code team rebuilt its code review around agents. Claude runs tests and builds, then a fresh agent reviews the change before anyone opens it. On each change, several agents hunt for bugs and others vote on each finding. A separate security pass runs, and a classifier sets how many people must approve.
how_it_went: The team reports merged changes more than doubled from June to September, while reverts fell by more than 40 percent. Most changes now merge with at most one human involved.
worth_knowing: They stress giving Claude a way to check its own work, like tests or a screenshot. Repeated reviewer complaints are fixed at the source in project instruction files.
prompt: Before I open a pull request for [repo], run the tests, build and linter and show me the output, not a summary. Then review the full change as a fresh reviewer, using [CLAUDE.md or review guide]. List each problem with a file and line as evidence, ranked by severity, starting with a count. Say plainly if there is nothing to fix. Suggest fixes, but wait for my approval before changing code or pushing anything.

source.name: Hacker News
source.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, Qing Wang

curation.rationale: Detailed first-party account of how agents check, review and gate code changes at high volume, with concrete numbers on merged changes and reverts. Very useful for any team using coding agents.
